content:
For some integer \(k\), the range
\[
\left(\frac{\omega\pi}{16}+\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{\omega\pi}{8}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
\]
must be contained in a negative-cosine interval
\[
\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi,\frac{3\pi}{2}+2k\pi\right).
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{\omega\pi}{16}+\frac{\pi}{4}\ge \frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\omega\ge 4+32k,
\]
and
\[
\frac{\omega\pi}{8}+\frac{\pi}{4}\le \frac{3\pi}{2}+2k\pi
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\omega\le 10+16k.
\]
So we need
\[
4+32k\le \omega\le 10+16k.
\]
This requires \(4+32k\le 10+16k\), so \(16k\le 6\), hence \(k\le 0\). Since \(\omega>0\), only \(k=0\) is possible, giving
\[
4\le \omega\le 10.
\]
Therefore, the maximum value is
\[
\boxed{10}.
\]
